findings.reason: Confirmed. I checked the owners table against the layer actions myself and the overloading is exactly as described. Five of the seven owner entries have a `formerly` naming a layer this proposal marks `narrow` — RG2.1, RG2.4 and RG2.5 twice, plus ShimuraData:D1 — and for those, 'formerly' does mean the content moved out. The other two name layers this proposal marks `keep`: entry 5, 'Group-scheme/functor-of-points dictionary used before local topologization', formerly RG2.0, and entry 6, 'Reductivity over a field ..., used on a special-fiber quotient', formerly RG2.3. So a consumer computing what each layer lost from owners[].formerly would read RG2.0 and RG2.3 as narrowed, against their own action field, and would carry away content those layers keep. The supporting evidence is accurate too: the narrowed layers carry `suppliedBy` and `keeps` while RG2.0 and RG2.3 carry neither, and both of their reasons say they are consuming the anchor's notions rather than losing content — RG2.0 'Use the upstream functor-of-points/group-scheme dictionary ...', RG2.3 'Use anchor group-scheme, quotient, unipotent-radical and reductivity notions: a supplied predicate is not a construction or proof of reductivity of this particular quotient.' The finding is careful not to overclaim: the substance is right in both cases and no layer is mis-scoped, only the encoding is ambiguous, and I agree. Low is the right severity and the fix is right and minimal — a `relation` field, or `usedBy` on those two entries — since as the finding notes both target strings already say 'used before ...' and 'used on ...', so only the machine-readable half is missing. I would make that change. I also re-ran the three attacks the report records as clean, because they bear on the finding's context: all 37 links resolve at both endpoints; every owner stage and every `formerly` stage resolves; and the proposed Part II title, 'Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models', is an exact prefix extension of the anchor's atlas title 'Reductive algebraic groups', so it obeys section 15 — and the report is right that this is a genuine improvement, since the atlas currently titles the roadmap 'Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models', which is not the anchor's title. Disclosure, since it is not a conflict the rules name but a reader should know: in a separate job (RT-AREA-representations-1) I relied on this proposal's owner entries 1 and 2 — the relative root system and relative Weyl group, and Bruhat/BN-pair theory, both moved to anchor Layer 7 — to decline reporting a duplication between ReductiveGroups Layer 7 and ReductiveGroupsPartII. Those two entries are among the five the finding classifies as genuine reassignments, correctly encoded, so this finding neither supports nor undermines that judgement; it concerns only entries 5 and 6, which I did not use.
